title: Mapungubwe
summary: Mapungubwe was southern Africa's first known kingdom, a trading state whose rulers lived on a hilltop above the Limpopo. Its gold, ivory and glass beads connected it to the Indian Ocean world.
caveat: Everything here comes from archaeology: there are no written records. Dates come from radiocarbon dating, and reasons for the rise and fall of these towns are interpretations.

stops.title: Schroda
stops.narration: The first big town in the valley grew rich trading ivory toward the coast. Clay figurines found here suggest initiation ceremonies.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows the national park; Schroda lies nearby.
sources: Thomas Huffman, Mapungubwe: Ancient African Civilisation on the Limpopo (2005)

stops.title: K2
stops.narration: The capital moved to a settlement now called K2, at the foot of the hill. Trade in glass beads and gold grew, and so did differences in wealth.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows the hill; K2 lies just beside it.
sources: Thomas Huffman, Mapungubwe: Ancient African Civilisation on the Limpopo (2005)

stops.title: Mapungubwe Hill
stops.narration: The ruler and elite moved to the top of the hill, separating themselves from commoners below. Archaeologists see this as the beginning of a class-based kingdom.
sources: Thomas Huffman, Mapungubwe: Ancient African Civilisation on the Limpopo (2005)

stops.title: Thulamela
stops.narration: A later stone-walled hilltop town to the east shows the Mapungubwe tradition spreading. Gold and trade goods were found in its royal graves.
stops.confidence_note: Thulamela was occupied for centuries; this date is its earliest phase.

stops.title: Great Zimbabwe
stops.narration: As Mapungubwe was abandoned, power shifted north to Great Zimbabwe, whose builders raised the largest ancient stone structures in Africa south of the Sahara.
stops.confidence_note: Why Mapungubwe declined, perhaps a drier climate or shifting trade routes, is debated.
sources: Thomas Huffman, Mapungubwe: Ancient African Civilisation on the Limpopo (2005)

stops.title: The golden rhinoceros
stops.narration: Royal graves on the hilltop were excavated, revealing a small rhinoceros of gold foil over a wooden core. It is kept, with the rest of the Mapungubwe Collection, at the University of Pretoria.
sources: Thomas Huffman, Mapungubwe: Ancient African Civilisation on the Limpopo (2005)
